title: Unify lightweight credential profiles and stream DSL ergonomics across SDKs
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) had diverging ergonomics for credential rotation, retry presets, and streaming consumer helpers. This caused production mismatches: transient 401s during stream resume and inconsistent retry windows across languages. This PR introduces a compact, cross-language 'CredentialProfile' concept plus a small stream DSL surface to harmonize retry/reauth behavior and improve developer ergonomics.

What this changes (summary):
- Introduces CredentialProfile (lightweight JSON-serializable spec) and a small runtime adapter in each SDK to select backoff/retry presets and prefetch behavior.
- Adds stream DSL helpers: typed pull/push iterables in TS, async iterator facade in Python, and slim iterator with context in Go to standardize resume and heartbeat hooks.
- Central compatibility shim in redwood/clients/sdk_compat to validate session headers during streaming handshakes.
- Version bumps: python -> 2.9.0, typescript -> 1.14.0, go -> 1.5.3.

Why this approach: Keeping the profiles lightweight lets product teams opt into automatic prefetching and credential warmup without changing low-level retry semantics. The stream DSL is intentionally minimal — a few helpers to reduce common boilerplate (resume_token, on_heartbeat, reauth_hook).

Files touched high-level: redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript, redwood-sdk-go, redwood/clients/sdk_compat, docs and CI pipeline.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked in Linear (ENG-11234, ENG-11235)
- [x] Implement CredentialProfile in all three SDKs
- [x] Add stream DSL helpers and adapters
- [x] E2E tests for stream resume with forced credential expiry
- [x] Migration docs and changelog entries
- [x] Version bumps and publish scripts

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests added in each SDK repo for profile parsing, backoff presets and reauth hook invocation.
- New CI job (pipeline-sdks.yaml) runs cross-language smoke test: spawn ephemeral server that simulates token expiry mid-stream; client must transparently reauthenticate and resume.
- Recorded a 48h dogfood run on staging Dedicated that exercised stream resume under load (latency/regression stats attached in PR checks).

Migration notes for integrators:
- CredentialProfile is backwards-compatible; if SDK config is omitted, SDKs default to legacy behavior.
- Recommended to adopt the new profile to get smoother resume and prefetch semantics; migration guide added at redwood/docs/sdk-migration/cred-profiles.md.

Rollback plan:
- Revert is scoped to SDK packages only; server compatibility shim is additive. If regressions surface, we can pin client-side versions and roll back publish tags while monitoring errors.

Related: SUP-4021 (customer incident that prompted tighter resume semantics), ENG-11234 (design), ENG-11235 (integration tests).

Aisha Patel (author): Added jitter tests and a backoff policy matrix test. Implemented explicit failure surface on reauth retry exhaustion; updated tests to assert error class.

Marta Gómez: Nice, but suggest renaming `prefetch_window` -> `warmup_window` for clarity in TS and Go APIs. Also request a short doc blurb showing how to combine CredentialProfile with existing per-call overrides.
Aisha Patel: Renamed field and added doc example in sdk-migration/cred-profiles.md. Kept python alias for backward compatibility for one release cycle.
Liam O'Connor: CI smoke runs looked good. One minor nit: add a comment in the Go iterator about context cancellation semantics to avoid future misuse.
Aisha Patel: Added comment and small test to validate cancellation stops the resume path immediately.
release_notes: Bumped SDK versions. Introduces CredentialProfile (compact auth/retry profile) and lightweight stream DSL helpers to harmonize stream resume and reauth behavior across Python/TS/Go. Backwards-compatible by default; see migration guide for opt-in instructions.
notes: This PR was coordinated with the infra team to add a short-lived CI image that can simulate token expiry. Publishing was gated until the e2e matrix passed for all three languages.
